source_supplementary.treatment: Completed forms uploaded as evidence; consolidated summary in the report (plan 5.4 assumption, D-039)

rules.message: Students who participated cannot exceed the students eligible.
Feedback responses cannot exceed the students who participated.

sections.title: Visit details
sections.intro: Department and academic year are filled from this report; the reporting period appears in the report summary.

fields.label: Academic Session / Year/ Semester (year of study and semester)
Number of students who participated
fields.help: As counted from the attendance record. KRA 19's target is a share of students per year; the portal does not calculate it.

fields.label: Number of students in the class/batch (optional)

sections.title: Profile of the Industry Visited (Brief Introduction)

fields.label: Profile of the Industry Visited
fields.guidance: Source prompts: Products/Services; Core Business Areas; Major Engineering Activities; Vision and Mission (if available); Organizational Structure.

fields.label: Detail of the Industry Experts (Interacted with)
Objectives of the industrial visit (one per line)
fields.guidance: Source: "Clearly state the objectives of the industrial visit." Typical objectives listed there: to expose students to real industrial environments; to understand practical engineering applications; to bridge the gap between theoretical concepts and industrial practices; to understand manufacturing, design, testing, maintenance, or operational processes; to observe industrial automation and digital technologies; to understand quality management and safety practices; to appreciate industrial professionalism and work culture.

fields.label: Technical Overview
fields.guidance: Source: "Provide a concise description of the major engineering activities carried out in the organization." Include: core technologies, engineering processes, automation systems, digital technologies, production philosophy, operational workflow.

fields.label: Departments and facilities visited (one record per department)

sections.title: Equipment, Quality/Safety and Environmental Practices
sections.intro: Describe only what was actually observed; write "Not observed" where a topic did not apply.

fields.label: Equipment and Technologies Observed
fields.guidance: Source examples: CNC Machines, Robotics, PLC-based Automation, SCADA Systems, Industrial IoT, Artificial Intelligence Applications, Machine Vision Systems, CAD/CAM Software, Testing Equipment, Quality Inspection Systems.

fields.label: Quality Assurance and Safety Practices
fields.guidance: Source prompts: quality inspection procedures, process monitoring, preventive maintenance, PPE, fire safety systems, emergency preparedness, occupational health practices, hazard identification, workplace safety culture.

fields.label: Environmental and Sustainability Practices
fields.guidance: Source prompts: waste management, water conservation, energy efficiency, pollution control measures, renewable energy utilization, green manufacturing practices, resource optimization.

fields.label: Key Learning Outcomes (one per line)
fields.guidance: Source: "Summarize the important learning gained through the visit." The report should reflect: practical understanding of engineering concepts, exposure to industrial technologies, appreciation of quality systems, understanding of professional ethics, awareness of industrial safety, teamwork and communication skills, knowledge of industrial best practices.

sections.title: Learning Outcome to PO/PSO mapping
sections.intro: One row per learning outcome. Cells are short text as used by the department (no scale is defined in the source; D-039). The source prints the last two columns as "PSO1" and "PSO1"; they are kept as printed pending the college's correction (D-012).

sections.title: Gap Fulfilment in Academics
sections.intro: Industrial visits can be used to bridge several academic gaps. Source examples: Theory-Practice Gap, Lack of AI Exposure, Sustainability Awareness, Innovation.

fields.label: Suggestions
fields.guidance: Source: constructive suggestions regarding future industrial visits, industry–academia collaboration, internship opportunities, laboratory improvements, skill development initiatives, emerging technology exposure.

fields.label: Conclusion
fields.guidance: Source: summarize the overall experience, highlighting the educational value of the visit, the enhancement of technical knowledge, exposure to industrial practices, and the role of such visits in preparing students for professional engineering careers.

fields.label: Faculty Coordinator Name (signature line stays blank)

sections.title: Industrial Visit Feedback (KRA 19b) — consolidated summary
sections.intro: Upload the completed student feedback forms in the Evidence tab (category "Student's Feedback"). Enter here only a consolidated summary; averages are optional and are never calculated by the portal (D-039).

fields.label: Consolidated average per feedback item (optional)
items: Industrial visit aligned with the course objectives and content.
Clarity of Explanation by Industry Experts

fields.label: Consolidated feedback summary
fields.help: Write "Not collected" if no feedback forms were collected for this visit.

sections.title: Annexures
sections.intro: The following supporting documents may be attached. Mark whether each is maintained; upload files in the Evidence tab.

evidence.note: No minimum evidence set has been agreed for KRA 19 (docs/decisions.md D-039). Completed 19b feedback forms belong under "Student's Feedback".
